newsitem.title: UK: Loading resumes at Sullom Voe Brent crude terminal.
newsitem.headline: Loading resumes at Sullom Voe Brent crude terminal.

text.p: Brent crude oil loadings resumed on Tuesday at the Sullom Voe oil terminal in the Shetland Islands ater being suspended at midnight on Monday because of high winds, the port manager there said.
"The 2.5 million barrel Jahra Polleux is currently loading. Loading was suspended but has now restarted," Jim Dickson said.

He said wind speeds reached 40 knots on Monday night and berthing was suspended. The winds had died down and three ships were waiting to berth but berthing has not resumed because the port operators had not given instructions for them.
"They are not berthing because there is no cargo for them," he said, adding that the winds were normal for this time of year.
"The Centaur has just left with half a million barrels and the winds are falling slowly. We expect normal operations by mid-day," Dickson said.
Gales and heavy rain lashed Britain overnight, injuring several people, blocking roads and leaving thousands of homes without power, emergency services said.
